llm.summary: The skill appears to do what it says (GitHub queries and issue creation) but the package/registry metadata omits the credential and config requirements described in SKILL.md and used by the code — a packaging/information mismatch you should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the implementation: the code talks only to api.github.com to list repos, check workflows, create issues, search, and read commits. Requiring a GitHub token/username is appropriate for these capabilities. However, the registry metadata declared no required env vars or primary credential while SKILL.md and index.js clearly expect/consume GITHUB_TOKEN and optionally GITHUB_USERNAME or an OpenClaw config entry.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the user to provide a GitHub PAT via environment variables or ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and to restart OpenClaw. The runtime instructions are limited to GitHub API operations and do not ask the agent to read unrelated system files, send data to unknown endpoints, or perform privileged local actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is present (instruction-only deployment with included JS code). There are no downloads from external/unknown URLs and package.json points to an expected repository. Risk from installation is low because nothing will be fetched or executed beyond the included index.js at runtime.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The code legitimately needs a GitHub token and supports reading GITHUB_TOKEN, GITHUB_USERNAME, or ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json. Those credential requirements are reasonable for GitHub integration, but the registry metadata lists no required env vars or primary credential and no required config paths — this mismatch can mislead users and automated review systems. The skill does not request unrelated credentials.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and the skill does not attempt to modify other skills or system-wide configuration. It only reads process.env and the provided OpenClaw config object; it does not persist tokens itself or create background services.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill's code and docs show it's a straightforward GitHub integration that needs a Personal Access Token (GITHUB_TOKEN) and optionally a username. However, the registry metadata incorrectly lists no required credentials/config — treat that as a packaging oversight. Before installing: 1) Confirm you trust the skill source (package.json repository and code). 2) Use a token with the minimal scopes you need (prefer public_repo for public-only or fine-grained tokens where possible). 3) Prefer a secrets manager or OpenClaw config rather than committing tokens to shell profiles. 4) After testing, rotate the token you used. If you need higher assurance, ask the publisher to correct the registry metadata to declare the required credentials and config paths, and review the repository history for unexpected changes.
